pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Urine changing to a port-wine color upon exposure to sunlight, paired with severe abdominal pain out of proportion to exam findings, acute ascending motor neuropathy, and severe hyponatremia triggered by caloric restriction. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: AIP is an autosomal dominant metabolic disorder caused by a partial deficiency of porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD) in the heme biosynthesis pathway. Severe dieting or fasting upregulates hepatic ALAS1 enzyme activity, causing a massive accumulation of toxic heme precursors, specifically delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG). Accumulation of these neurotoxins damages the autonomic, peripheral, and central nervous systems, leading to severe abdominal pain, autonomic instability, flaccid paralysis, hyponatremia via SIADH, and psychiatric symptoms. PBG oxidizes to porphobilin in the presence of light and air, producing the characteristic dark urine.
